deities: All deities of the Sanatan Dharma pantheon (idols enshrined throughout)

history.summary: Solid entry: one of the famous religious landmarks of Rewari, a three-storied temple in the heart of the city (Gokal Bazar / Purani Subji Mandi Road, Kumharo Mohalla / Kayasthwara Mohalla). Its distinctive feature is that idols of all the gods and goddesses of Sanatan Dharma are established here. A Shivstuti (invocation to Lord Shiva) composed by Ali Bakesh is engraved on a marble slab at the temple's entrance. NOTE on the brief's ghanta-Rewari etymology: the CSV detail hint linked the town's name 'Rewari' to this temple's bells (ghanta); no web source was found confirming this, so treat it as an unverified local tradition. Built date undocumented. CSV town/state error: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name ('Rewari'); the correct state is Haryana.

name: Ghanteshwar Temple
town_description: Rewari is a historic city in southern Haryana and the administrative centre of Rewari district, about 80 km southwest of Delhi. An old Ahirwal trading town with a famous steam-locomotive shed museum, it is a major railway junction and a fast-growing NCR industrial hub.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 90 km from Rewari.
travel.railway: Rewari Junction is the nearest major railway station.
travel.road: In the city centre - Moti Chowk / Gokal Bazar, Purani Subji Mandi Road, Kumharo Mohalla (5JX7+GH2, Kayasthwara Mohalla), Rewari 123401.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivratri is the main festival.
